# Plan Your Visit 參觀指南

Asia’s first global museum of visual culture in Hong Kong’s WestK is open Tuesday through Sunday.

![View of one level of an atrium with black railings of the walkways stretching across the frame. A spiral staircase in the centre rises through the concrete ceiling, which is illuminated by lines of fluorescent lights. Two diagonal sections of mega-trusses angled towards the centre stand on each side of the staircase. The walkway at the far end leads to entrances to an enclosed area.](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)

## Admission 入場

[Get Tickets   Get Tickets   Get Tickets](/en/get-tickets/)

Welcome to M+! Explore free spaces of the museum, or purchase tickets for more access. ​

Access to the [Mediatheque](/en/mediatheque/), the Grand Stair (except for ticketed events), B1, B2, Found Space, and the Roof Garden remains free.

[Become a Member](/en/membership/) today to enjoy unlimited admission to all galleries and exhibitions, discounts, and many other exclusive benefits. See ‘M+ Members and Patrons’ for details.

**M+ Ticket**

Standard: **HKD 190**  
Concessions\*: **HKD 100**  
Kid & Adult Combo - 2-person set (1 Adult + 1 Kid) #: **HKD 250**  
Kid & Adult Combo - 3-person set (2 Adult + 1 Kid) #: **HKD 400**

M+ Members and Patrons can enjoy exclusive benefits and discounts.  
  
Children ages 6 and below do not need a ticket.  
  
\*Concession tickets are available to full-time students, children ages 7 to 11, senior citizens ages 60 or above, person with disabilities and one companion, and Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA) recipients.

**M+ Members and Patrons** can enjoy a wide range of exclusive benefits, and each unique membership status comes with its own level of privileges that elevate your experience at M+.

Unlimited admission to all galleries and exhibitions is available at all membership levels.  
  
**M+ Patrons**, **Young Patrons** and **Affiliates** may enjoy the following exhibition benefits:

* Free admission with three guests during museum’s opening hours and [M+ Private Viewing](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/events/mplus-private-viewing/) hours. No prior booking required.
* Priority lane access at the entrances of the exhibitions with accompanied guests. The first three guests can enjoy free access, additional guests will require a valid ticket.
* A 50% discount on standard tickets.

M+ supporters at the **Council**, **Benefactor**, and **Director's Circle** levels are entitled to additional benefits in recognition of their extraordinary generosity.

➔ Learn more and [Become a Member](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/membership/) today!

Join our tours to explore our exhibitions in greater depth.

➔ [Groups and Tours](/en/groups-and-tours/)

➔ [School Visit Request](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/school-visit-request/)

[Summer at M+   Summer at M+   Summer at M+](/en/plan-your-visit/summer-at-mplus/)

Lights suspended by four rods that meet at the top of dome lampshades hang from the ceiling of the entranceway. Columns of tubular terracotta tiles form undulating panels on the building's facade, stretching across and occupying two thirds of the frame from the top.](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)

## Opening Hours 開放時間

**Tuesdays to Thursdays and Sundays:** 10:00–18:00 **Fridays:** 10:00–22:00

**Saturdays\*:** 10:00–20:00 **Mondays:** ClosedThe last admission time is thirty minutes before closing.  
  
The museum is open on all public holidays unless otherwise announced.

**Special Arrangement:**

\*M+’s opening hours on Saturdays are extended to 20:00 from 4 July to 29 August 2026.

Please stay tuned to the announcements on the M+ website for updates during inclement weather conditions.

**Amber or Red Rainstorm Warning / Typhoon Signal No. 1 or No. 3**

* The museum will remain open, but outdoor exhibitions and events may be suspended.

**Black Rainstorm Warning**

* If hoisted before opening hours: The museum will remain closed until the signal is lowered. The museum will re-open three hours after the signal is lowered. If the signal is cancelled or lowered less than four hours from the normal closing time, the museum will remain closed for the rest of the day.
* If hoisted during opening hours: The museum will remain open with limited operations. All outdoor exhibitions and events will be suspended.
* In the above two situations, the validity of unused M+ tickets will be extended for 60 days starting from the day of the inclement weather. Visitor can retain and bring the original tickets for admission at the same time slot within the validity period. Please call (852) 2200 0217 for inquiries.

**Typhoon Signal No. 8 or above**

* If hoisted before opening hours: The museum will remain closed until the signal is lowered. The museum will re-open three hours after the signal is lowered. If the signal is cancelled or lowered less than four hours from the normal closing time, the museum will remain closed for the rest of the day.
* If hoisted during opening hours: The museum will be closed.
* In the above two situations, the validity of M+ tickets will be extended for 60 days starting from the day of the inclement weather. Visitor can retain and bring the original tickets for admission at the same time slot within the validity period. Please call (852) 2200 0217 for inquiries.

Some venues in the museum may have different operating hours in times of inclement weather. Please check with the individual venues for the most up-to-date information.

The Research Centre is available by appointment only during **Tuesdays to Thursdays** from 10:00–17:00.

➔ [Learn More](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/research-centre/)

![View of a slender grey tower rising from a podium in the centre, beside a campus of buildings on the viewer's left. The tower stands behind a park with a path in the centre leading through grassy areas and trees. In the foreground, children cycle on the road towards the left.](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)

## Tips for Visiting 參觀提示

Bags and backpacks smaller than 30 cm x 42 cm x 10 cm are allowed in the galleries, but backpacks must be worn on the front of the body with the strap(s) slung over one or both shoulders. Larger items must be checked in to lockers or the cloakroom, available for rental.

We welcome wheelchairs and baby strollers in the galleries. These are also available to borrow free of charge on a first-come, first-served basis.  
  
M+ offers free audio guides. For the best in-gallery experience, listen on your mobile via [audioguide.mplus.org.hk](https://audioguide.mplus.org.hk/) with a headset.

Key in the audio stop number or scan the QR code on the object labels in the M+ galleries. Listen to interviews and audio description of the objects through Cantonese, English, and Mandarin audio tracks. Headsets and mobile devices are available to borrow. Please visit the Ground Floor Information Desk for full details.  
  
➔ [Access the in-gallery audio guide using your mobile device](https://audioguide.mplus.org.hk/)  
  
➔ [Explore our archived audio guide content](/en/audio-guide/)

Ticket holders can join a free 30–45 minutes tour to learn more about the museum, the M+ Collections and/or the special exhibitions currently on view.​  
  
Public tours—held either in Cantonese, English, or Mandarin—take place from Tuesdays to Sundays. The schedule, theme, and language of each tour may vary.​

​

➔ [Find out more about our public tours​](/en/groups-and-tours/)

* Ensure the flash is turned off when taking photos. Video recording is only permitted when specified. Professional photography or videography for commercial use must be arranged in advance.
* Please be respectful to all M+ staff and other visitors.
* Smoking, including the consumption of e-cigarettes, is restricted to a designated area at the Roof Garden on L3.
* Food and drinks can only be consumed in cafes and restaurants.
* Please help us take care of the objects on view in the museum. Do not touch the works on display unless otherwise specified. Maintain a safe distance from all works, cases, platforms, and pedestals.
* With the exception of service dogs, animals are not permitted in the museum.
* As a safety measure to protect all visitors and staff members, visitors may get their personal belongings, clothing, and other items screened.

If your driver requires assistance, ask your driver to head to the roundabout at Nga Cheung Road and Austin Road West and head to Museum Drive. At the first intersection on Museum Drive, on your left is a designated pick-up and drop-off area. This will also take you to the B1 entrance of the Museum.

Parking is available at WestK.

Parking is available at the [M+ Car Park](https://www.westk.hk/en/parking), which can be accessed from the driveway to the museum’s pick-up and drop-off area on 38 Museum Drive. You can also park at the Art Park Car Park. Street parking is unavailable in WestK.

## Moving Image Centre 流動影像中心

The Moving Image Centre consists of the M+ Cinema, Grand Stair, and Mediatheque. You can access the Moving Image Centre via the Waterfront Promenade Entrance on B1, the East Entrance on G, or B1 entrances after the museum is closed.

Come and explore the wide variety of screening programmes at the [M+ Cinema](/en/cinema/), [Grand Stair,](/en/events/) and [Mediatheque](/en/mediatheque/).

## WestK 西九文化區

WestK is one of the largest and most ambitious cultural projects in the world. Its vision is to create a vibrant new cultural quarter for Hong Kong on forty hectares of reclaimed land located alongside Victoria Harbour. With a mix of theatres, performance spaces, and museums, WestK produces and hosts world-class exhibitions, performances, and cultural events. When complete, it will provide twenty-three hectares of public open space, including a two-kilometre waterfront promenade.

Currently open to the public are the Hong Kong Palace Museum, Xiqu Centre, Freespace, and the Art Park. The WestK Performing Arts Centre is scheduled to be completed in 2026.

Please note taht Kowloon Station/Elements is not connected to TST, which is the "central" shopping area on the Kowloon side. You will need to take a (5 minute) taxi to get you between these two locations. As most of my meetings were on the Hong Kong Island side, I had to take the train to Hong Kong station and walk to connect to Central Station, which is about a 700m underground walk. The entire trip from the hotel to Central station on the Hong Kong side probably takes 20 minutes. [...] The W is what you'd expect from a W. It's hip, chic and modern. It caters to a younger, trendier crowd, and if you want quiet and reserved, the W is not for you. The "woobar" at the lobby level (6F) always seems crowded with smartly dressed people, and a loud thumping beat emits from it throughout the evening. Because it's connected to ICC and Elements, the dining and shopping options are endless. 

The rooms are modern and simply laid out. The standard rooms are 40 sqm, and one will find all the modern ammenities in the room. The stero controls were a bit difficult for me the first time, probably as I'm not very good with technology. My pet peeve with the layout of the rooms is that the bathrooms are open and don't have a door. [...] Turkish (1)

# Convenient location above Airport Express and MTR station

Review of [W Hong Kong](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Hotel_Review-g294217-d1068719-Reviews-W_Hong_Kong-Hong_Kong.html)

Reviewed Apr 3, 2013

Stayed here for a work week in March. This was my third stay here. The W is located right above the Kowloon Station (for Airport Express and MTR) in a development called "Elements" and is easily accessible to/from the airport. Please note taht Kowloon Station/Elements is not connected to TST, which is the "central" shopping area on the Kowloon side. You will need to take a (5 minute) taxi to get you between these two locations. As most of my meetings were on the Hong Kong Island side, I had to take the train to Hong Kong station and walk to connect to Central Station, which is about a 700m underground walk. The entire trip from the hotel to Central station on the Hong Kong side probably takes 20 minutes.

The W is what you'd expect from a W. It's hip, chic and modern. It caters to a younger, trendier crowd, and if you want quiet and reserved, the W is not for you. The "woobar" at the lobby level (6F) always seems crowded with smartly dressed people, and a loud thumping beat emits from it throughout the evening. Because it's connected to ICC and Elements, the dining and shopping options are endless. 

The rooms are modern and simply laid out. The standard rooms are 40 sqm, and one will find all the modern ammenities in the room. The stero controls were a bit difficult for me the first time, probably as I'm not very good with technology. My pet peeve with the layout of the rooms is that the bathrooms are open and don't have a door. 

I only had two breakfasts at the hotel. One was the buffet breakfast at "Kitchen" on the lobby level; the wide assortment of breakfast items, including both western and Asian dishes, can satisfy any craving. I also had room service one morning and the food was also not bad.

All in alll a decent hotel if one doesn't mind being in Kowloon.

I booked a cool corner room; the room is comfortable but the view is just.. so-so. If you are looking for a really nice corner view room, East Hotel will be a much better choice. 

The corner of the writing desk got a small triangle spider web. I was a little shocked, but the housekeeping staff kept apologize to me and they let me changed to another room. 

The staff is kind and polite, but it's a normal standard for 4-5 stars Hong Kong hotels.

The high tea is delicious. The quality has exceeded my expectation. In fact, it's much than the Ritz carlton's both 102/F and 103/F high tea which is just next to W hotel. Highly recommended the high tea.

The design of the hotel and the room is trendy and chic overall, but I have stayed and have seen many other trendier and more chic hotels. It's still suitable for SPG members and business travellers who need to work in ICC.

Room tip: Higher floors have less noise and better sea view I guess.

[BAD EXPERIENCE](https://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g294217-d1068719-r156073068-W_Hong_Kong-Hong_Kong.html)

We planned to spend 5 nights in Hong Kong W hotel. We have choosen this hotel because of the positive advices from Tripadvisor. Our disappointment was great.

The hotel is located in the middle of nowhere. The link to civilization is the magnificent Mall and the MTR Kowloon station.

We booked a fabulous room. As soon we entered the room we felt bad. The fabulous room has a fabulous view over the highway with lot of traffic. The view over the harbour was also awful. Since the room was very noisy we asked to change for another one. We had a Spectacular room (less expensive) a little bit less noisy. The room was quite confortable despite the noise.

The lobby and the Kitchen restaurant are also noisy. Music shoul be not so loud, maybe it is a W trend because the W bangkok is suffering same noisy attitude. Kitchen restaurant has the same "fabulous" view on the harbour. No yachts or fishboats, only offload barges!

Staff was kind and helpful. Breakfast is typically american style. Don't expect too much asian food. There are much more bagels than nooddles!

We missed an outdoor terrace with some shelter in case of rainy day. But it seems to be common in Hong kong hotels.

We left 2 nights earlier because we couldn't afford much more a such bad experience.

Disappointment was as high as the room rate!

Room tip: Standard room are certainly quieter than the fabulous.

**4) Taxi Services**Citizens and tourists can choose to take ordinary taxis and fleet taxis.  
  
Access to pick-up area for urban taxis  
  
Citizens and tourists without taxi booking can follow directional signs to the pick-up area for urban taxis at B2 floor of Hong Kong West Kowloon Station. The drop-off area is located at B1 floor of the Station. [Fare table](https://www.td.gov.hk/en/transport_in_hong_kong/public_transport/taxi/taxi_fare_of_hong_kong/index.html) is displayed inside the vehicles for passengers' information.

Booking of fleet taxis

Citizens and tourists can also book [taxi fleet](https://www.td.gov.hk/en/transport_in_hong_kong/public_transport/taxi/tfli2024/index.html) service in West Kowloon Station.

To facilitate the fleet taxis to pick up the passengers with pre-booked trips, the Transport Department sets up 8 stopping places designated for fleet taxis in the **carpark on B2/F** and **outside Exit B on G/F** of the West Kowloon Station. Passengers can specify the pick-up location when booking fleet.

QR codes of the booking services provided by taxi fleets are also displayed at the stopping places to facilitate booking by the citizens and tourists.

**Traffic and Transport Facilities**

**1) Station Pick-up / Drop-off area**

The vehicular entrance (headroom limit 3.1 metres) of Hong Kong West Kowloon Station is located at the loop road on Lin Cheung Road (southbound). Motorists may take the following routes to access Hong Kong West Kowloon Station (Note 2):

| (iii) | For motorists from the New Territories via West Kowloon Highway, they may use Lin Cheung Road (southbound)  (video clip [WMV format](/filemanager/en/content_4910/hkwks_xrl_r3_wmv_eng.wmv)  [MP4 format](/filemanager/en/content_4910/hkwks_xrl_r3_mp4_eng.mp4)  [Script version](/filemanager/en/content_4910/hkwks_xrl_r3_script_eng.pdf)) . |

The Station drop-off area is located at B1 floor (ticketing concourse) of Hong Kong West Kowloon Station. There is a Station car park, including pick-up/ drop-off points and about 500 private car parking spaces, at B2 floor (arrival concourse) for public use. A pick-up/drop-off area is also provided at Wui Man Road (northbound).

Note 2: Motorists should plan their journeys ahead and watch out for the latest traffic news and temporary traffic arrangement through various media channels, e.g. radio traffic news and the Transport Department's mobile application "HKeMobility".

**2) Non-franchised Bus Pick-up / Drop-off area**

Non-franchised buses can access Hong Kong West Kowloon Station via Wui Cheung Road (westbound) or Wui Man Road (southbound) and make use of the designated area for non-franchised buses on Wui Man Road for picking up and dropping off passengers. Vehicle waiting is prohibited.

There are 30 metered parking spaces for non-franchised buses near the West Kowloon Station Bus Terminus. Since vehicle waiting is prohibited at the above non-franchised bus pick-up/drop-off area on Wui Man Road, non-franchised buses can use the parking spaces for short-term parking.

**3) Pedestrian Facilities**

Hong Kong West Kowloon Station is connected by pedestrian footbridges and subways to the nearby public transport facilities, including Austin Station, West Kowloon Station Bus Terminus, and through a shopping mall to Kowloon Station and Kowloon Station Public Transport Interchange.

Commuters walking along Jordan Road in Yau Ma Tei and Canton Road in Tsim Sha Tsui may gain access to Hong Kong West Kowloon Station via its nearby subways and through Austin Station, while commuters from Jordan Road and Austin Road West near Kowloon Station may make use of the footpaths and footbridges nearby to go to Hong Kong West Kowloon Station.

**Advice to Visitors**

**1) General Advice to Visitors heading for Hong Kong West Kowloon Station**

Visitors should pay attention to the departure time of High Speed Rail train to ensure that there is adequate time to complete the departure procedures.

To avoid the peak hours, visitors should plan their trips well in advance and check the latest traffic and public transport information through various media channels, e.g. radio traffic news, and the Transport Department's mobile application "HKeMobility".

## What is the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The M+ Museum or MPlus is one of the latest sightseeing attractions. Opened on November 12, 2021 at the West Kowloon Cultural District, it is the first museum of modern and contemporary visual culture in Asia. And also one of the largest in the world. The museum is one of the world-class facilities in Hong Kong.

![Mplus Museum in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Logo of the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

The logo of the M+ Museum

This world-class museum showcases 20th and 21st century visual culture on 17,000 square meters. 33 galleries and 3 cinema houses wait to be explored and discovered. So, make sure to plan sufficient time when visiting this excellent museum.

### Architecture of the M+ Museum

The impressive museum of modern and contemporary visual culture is already visible from far distance. The slender 18-storey building has been designed by famous Herzog & de Meuron, TFP Farrells and Arup. Needless to say that the MPlus immediately became one of the iconic buildings of the city.

It is situated just next to the Hong Kong Palace Museum. In close proximity is also the city’s tallest building – the International Commerce Centre (ICC), where you will also find sky100 – the highest observation deck in town.

![Stunning modern and contemporary design of the Mplus Museum in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The design and architecture of the M+ Museum Hong Kong")

Modern and contemporary design

Taking a closer look at this elegant and impressive building, you might be reminded of an upside-down ‘T’ shape. The building combines modern construction elements, space and lighting concepts with traditional Chinese and local elements.

The facade is e.g. inspired by traditional Chinese roofs. In fact, the facade uses custom-designed cladding, some made of terracotta. Other unique elements throughout the building include different textured wood and concretes highlighting the use of durable materials.

![Stunning modern and contemporary design of the Mplus Museum in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The design and architecture of the M+ Museum Hong Kong")

Make sure to admire the design and architecture of this museum

In addition, the facade of the M+ building consists of 5,664 LED tubes. The giant screen is facing [Victoria Harbour](https://www.nextstophongkong.com/victoria-harbor/ "Famous Victoria Harbour - Everything you need to know about this must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong") and can be seen from far distance.

![Hong Kong Mplus Museum and the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "West Kowloon Cultural District and M+ Museum")

The facade of the museum and the West Kowloon Cultural District can be seen from Hong Kong Island

The impressive M+ facade functions not only as an innovate digital exhibition space. It is also part of the nightly [A Symphony of Lights and Laser](https://www.nextstophongkong.com/symphony-of-lights/ "Where to watch and enjoy A Symphony of Lights and Laser show in Hong Kong - Everything you need to know about this must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong") attraction show. It is visible from the Kowloon as well as Hong Kong Island side.

The design concept of the museum reflects art and modernity. Needless to say that the newly building itself became with an blink of an eye one of the city’s famous landmarks. In addition, it is one of the recent Instagram and selfie hotspots.

## Highlights of the Hong Kong M+ Museum

The MPlus houses a large range of exhibitions and art collections. The art works have been collected primarily from Hong Kong, Mainland China and the rest of Asia. But you also can find artists and their works from the rest of the world. One highlight of the visual culture collection is to showcase the interdisciplinary of different fields of art. Explore and discover some of the world’s best art works of architecture, design and moving images. So, let’s take a closer look.

![Mplus Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "World-class M+ Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong")

The world class MPlus Museum

### Permanent Exhibitions

The MPlus has 4 collections that are permanently on display. Currently, there are over 6,700 art pieces, items and objects. The collections have been structured in the following 4 permanent exhibitions:

#### – Design and Architecture

This collection focuses on 20th and 21st-century design and architecture. The exhibition features primarily work from Hong Kong and Asia. Among thousands of objects, you can admire e.g. posters, textiles, fashion, furniture, electronics and of course architecture and interior designs.

#### – Moving Image

The Moving Image collection focuses on the development of films over the last two centuries. The collection is very broad and covers a wide range of objects. These include e.g. animations, video games, videos, movies, digital art installations and even web-based works.

#### – Visual Art

The Visual Art collection is for all who love photographs, prints and sculptures. This collection feature a wide spectrum of modern and contemporary drawings, paintings and live art.

#### – Hong Kong Visual Culture

The fourth permanent collection focuses on Hong Kong. The collection objects are from various disciplines and fields of arts.

### Special Thematic Exhibitions

Another highlight of the MPlus Museum are the regular changing Special Exhibitions. These exhibitions are just temporarily available. They focus on specific art topics, artists or specific works. Below are some of the most popular exhibitions of the past:

* Madame Song: Pioneering Art and Fashion in China
* M+ Sigg Collection: From revolution to Globalisation
* Yayoi Kusama: Pumpkin
* Hong Kong: Here and Beyond
* Beeple: HUMAN ONE
* Angela Su: Arise, Hong Kong in Venice
* Young-Hae Chang: Heavy Industries
* Yayoi Kusama: 1945 to Now

## What can you do at the MPlus Museum?

The permanent and special exhibitions are not the only things you can do at the HKMP. Besides the 33 galleries, the museum also houses the Moving Image Centre. This centre consists of 3 cinemas houses (40, 60 and 180 seats), Grand Stair and a Mediatheque.

![Popular Hong Kong M+ Museum provides plenty of things to explore and discover](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Take a seat and relax at the MPlus Museum")

Besides the exhibition halls and the cinemas, there is a roof top garden and the M+ Playscape. The rooftop garden offers beautiful views of Victoria Harbour. Visitors can rest on the benches at the M+ Playscape and enjoy the sculptures from famous designer Isamu Noguchi.

![The sky100 Observation Deck next to the MPlus Museum is another popular sightseeing attraction at the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Close to the museum is the sky100 Observation Deck inside the ICC building")

The museum is close to the sky100 Observation Deck inside the ICC

Moreover, there is e.g. a learning hub, restaurants, cafés and a gift shop with some unique products and souvenirs. Furthermore, the museum organises e.g. special lectures, guided tours, workshops, talks, performances, movie screening and activities.

### How much is M+ Museum ticket?

So, how much are the ticket prices, entrance fees and admissions to the Hong Kong M+ Museum? Ticket prices and entrance fees depends which part and galleries of the museum you want to visit.

#### – General Admission tickets

Ticket prices for the permanent thematic Exhibitions Halls are:

* Standard Ticket – HKD 120
* Concession Ticket – HKD 60 (Children age 7 to 11, full-time students, seniors age 60+, people with disabilities and CSSA recipients))

#### – Ticket prices for the Special Thematic Exhibitions

In case you would like to visit and explore the special thematic exhibitions (e.g. Madame Song: Pioneering Art and Fashion in China), you need to purchase tickets for the Special Exhibitions Galleries. These tickets also include a General Admission ticket. Hence, you can enter and enjoy the exhibitions of the whole museum.

Ticket prices for the Special Exhibitions are:

* Standard Ticket – HKD 140
* Concession Ticket – HKD 70 (Children age 7 to 11, full-time students, seniors age 60+, people with disabilities and CSSA recipients))
* M+ Members – HKD 98
* M+ Patrons’ Guests – HKD 70

## Is it worthwhile to visit the M+ Museum?

The M+ Museum is highly recommended not only if you love or are interested in modern art, design and architecture. Focusing on various disciplines as well as having thematic collections such as e.g. Hong Kong’s visual culture makes this museum a must-visit.

![Hong Kong MPlus Museum is not only a popular place to visit for modern art lovers](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The M+ Museum is a must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong")

Enjoy the architecture of the museum and stunning harbour views

The large collections are very well curated. Interactive exhibits, latest technologies (e.g. use mobile devices to interact with the collections), M+ Playscape, the gigantic outdoor LED screen all add to the overall experience and make it worthwhile to visit.

Furthermore, the contemporary designed building itself is an highlight. Especially, if you are interested in design and architecture, you should not miss this unique landmark. There is plenty to discover inside and outside.

![MPlus Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "World-class M+ Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong")

The world class MPlus Museum

So, if you have visited MoMA in New York or the Tate Modern in London, you will enjoy and love this museum. In fact, this world-class museum doesn’t need to hide. Having said that, the M+ Museum is a must-visit and not only a great choice on a rainy day. Expect to stay the whole day.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

![Follow the signs to get to the Mplus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Sign leading to the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Sign leading the way

Another option is to leave the Kowloon MTR station through Exit E4 or E5. Walk along Nga Cheung Road. Then cross the footbridge and follow the signs to the museum.

![The MPlus Museum can be reached via the harbour crossing footbridge](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "To reach the Hong Kong M+ Museum you have to cross the footbridge")

Cross the footbridge

### By MTR then use free shuttle bus

Alternatively, you can take the MTR subway and travel to the Austin MTR station and take Exit D. From there you can hop on the free shuttle bus taking you to the museum district. The free shuttle bus departs every 20 minutes.

![Take Exit D at MTR Austin station to enjoy free shuttle bus service to the MPlus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Free shuttle bus service to Hong Kong M+ Museum from MTR Austin Station Exit D")

MTR notice for free shuttle bus at Exit D

## What is the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The M+ Museum or MPlus is one of the latest sightseeing attractions. Opened on November 12, 2021 at the West Kowloon Cultural District, it is the first museum of modern and contemporary visual culture in Asia. And also one of the largest in the world. The museum is one of the world-class facilities in Hong Kong.

![Mplus Museum in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Logo of the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

The logo of the M+ Museum

This world-class museum showcases 20th and 21st century visual culture on 17,000 square meters. 33 galleries and 3 cinema houses wait to be explored and discovered. So, make sure to plan sufficient time when visiting this excellent museum.

### Architecture of the M+ Museum

The impressive museum of modern and contemporary visual culture is already visible from far distance. The slender 18-storey building has been designed by famous Herzog & de Meuron, TFP Farrells and Arup. Needless to say that the MPlus immediately became one of the iconic buildings of the city.

It is situated just next to the Hong Kong Palace Museum. In close proximity is also the city’s tallest building – the International Commerce Centre (ICC), where you will also find sky100 – the highest observation deck in town.

![Stunning modern and contemporary design of the Mplus Museum in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The design and architecture of the M+ Museum Hong Kong")

Modern and contemporary design

Taking a closer look at this elegant and impressive building, you might be reminded of an upside-down ‘T’ shape. The building combines modern construction elements, space and lighting concepts with traditional Chinese and local elements.

The facade is e.g. inspired by traditional Chinese roofs. In fact, the facade uses custom-designed cladding, some made of terracotta. Other unique elements throughout the building include different textured wood and concretes highlighting the use of durable materials.

![Stunning modern and contemporary design of the Mplus Museum in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The design and architecture of the M+ Museum Hong Kong")

Make sure to admire the design and architecture of this museum

In addition, the facade of the M+ building consists of 5,664 LED tubes. The giant screen is facing [Victoria Harbour](https://www.nextstophongkong.com/victoria-harbor/ "Famous Victoria Harbour - Everything you need to know about this must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong") and can be seen from far distance.

![Hong Kong Mplus Museum and the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "West Kowloon Cultural District and M+ Museum")

The facade of the museum and the West Kowloon Cultural District can be seen from Hong Kong Island

The impressive M+ facade functions not only as an innovate digital exhibition space. It is also part of the nightly [A Symphony of Lights and Laser](https://www.nextstophongkong.com/symphony-of-lights/ "Where to watch and enjoy A Symphony of Lights and Laser show in Hong Kong - Everything you need to know about this must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong") attraction show. It is visible from the Kowloon as well as Hong Kong Island side.

The design concept of the museum reflects art and modernity. Needless to say that the newly building itself became with an blink of an eye one of the city’s famous landmarks. In addition, it is one of the recent Instagram and selfie hotspots.

## Highlights of the Hong Kong M+ Museum

The MPlus houses a large range of exhibitions and art collections. The art works have been collected primarily from Hong Kong, Mainland China and the rest of Asia. But you also can find artists and their works from the rest of the world. One highlight of the visual culture collection is to showcase the interdisciplinary of different fields of art. Explore and discover some of the world’s best art works of architecture, design and moving images. So, let’s take a closer look.

![Mplus Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "World-class M+ Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong")

The world class MPlus Museum

### Permanent Exhibitions

The MPlus has 4 collections that are permanently on display. Currently, there are over 6,700 art pieces, items and objects. The collections have been structured in the following 4 permanent exhibitions:

#### – Design and Architecture

This collection focuses on 20th and 21st-century design and architecture. The exhibition features primarily work from Hong Kong and Asia. Among thousands of objects, you can admire e.g. posters, textiles, fashion, furniture, electronics and of course architecture and interior designs.

#### – Moving Image

The Moving Image collection focuses on the development of films over the last two centuries. The collection is very broad and covers a wide range of objects. These include e.g. animations, video games, videos, movies, digital art installations and even web-based works.

#### – Visual Art

The Visual Art collection is for all who love photographs, prints and sculptures. This collection feature a wide spectrum of modern and contemporary drawings, paintings and live art.

#### – Hong Kong Visual Culture

The fourth permanent collection focuses on Hong Kong. The collection objects are from various disciplines and fields of arts.

### Special Thematic Exhibitions

Another highlight of the MPlus Museum are the regular changing Special Exhibitions. These exhibitions are just temporarily available. They focus on specific art topics, artists or specific works. Below are some of the most popular exhibitions of the past:

* Madame Song: Pioneering Art and Fashion in China
* M+ Sigg Collection: From revolution to Globalisation
* Yayoi Kusama: Pumpkin
* Hong Kong: Here and Beyond
* Beeple: HUMAN ONE
* Angela Su: Arise, Hong Kong in Venice
* Young-Hae Chang: Heavy Industries
* Yayoi Kusama: 1945 to Now

## Is it worthwhile to visit the M+ Museum?

The M+ Museum is highly recommended not only if you love or are interested in modern art, design and architecture. Focusing on various disciplines as well as having thematic collections such as e.g. Hong Kong’s visual culture makes this museum a must-visit.

![Hong Kong MPlus Museum is not only a popular place to visit for modern art lovers](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The M+ Museum is a must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong")

Enjoy the architecture of the museum and stunning harbour views

The large collections are very well curated. Interactive exhibits, latest technologies (e.g. use mobile devices to interact with the collections), M+ Playscape, the gigantic outdoor LED screen all add to the overall experience and make it worthwhile to visit.

Furthermore, the contemporary designed building itself is an highlight. Especially, if you are interested in design and architecture, you should not miss this unique landmark. There is plenty to discover inside and outside.

![MPlus Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "World-class M+ Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong")

The world class MPlus Museum

So, if you have visited MoMA in New York or the Tate Modern in London, you will enjoy and love this museum. In fact, this world-class museum doesn’t need to hide. Having said that, the M+ Museum is a must-visit and not only a great choice on a rainy day. Expect to stay the whole day.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

![Follow the signs to get to the Mplus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Sign leading to the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Sign leading the way

Another option is to leave the Kowloon MTR station through Exit E4 or E5. Walk along Nga Cheung Road. Then cross the footbridge and follow the signs to the museum.

## What can you do at the MPlus Museum?

The permanent and special exhibitions are not the only things you can do at the HKMP. Besides the 33 galleries, the museum also houses the Moving Image Centre. This centre consists of 3 cinemas houses (40, 60 and 180 seats), Grand Stair and a Mediatheque.

![Popular Hong Kong M+ Museum provides plenty of things to explore and discover](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Take a seat and relax at the MPlus Museum")

Take a seat and relax

Besides the exhibition halls and the cinemas, there is a roof top garden and the M+ Playscape. The rooftop garden offers beautiful views of Victoria Harbour. Visitors can rest on the benches at the M+ Playscape and enjoy the sculptures from famous designer Isamu Noguchi.

![The sky100 Observation Deck next to the MPlus Museum is another popular sightseeing attraction at the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Close to the museum is the sky100 Observation Deck inside the ICC building")

The museum is close to the sky100 Observation Deck inside the ICC

Moreover, there is e.g. a learning hub, restaurants, cafés and a gift shop with some unique products and souvenirs. Furthermore, the museum organises e.g. special lectures, guided tours, workshops, talks, performances, movie screening and activities.

## Is it worthwhile to visit the M+ Museum?

The M+ Museum is highly recommended not only if you love or are interested in modern art, design and architecture. Focusing on various disciplines as well as having thematic collections such as e.g. Hong Kong’s visual culture makes this museum a must-visit.

![Hong Kong MPlus Museum is not only a popular place to visit for modern art lovers](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The M+ Museum is a must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong")

Enjoy the architecture of the museum and stunning harbour views

The large collections are very well curated. Interactive exhibits, latest technologies (e.g. use mobile devices to interact with the collections), M+ Playscape, the gigantic outdoor LED screen all add to the overall experience and make it worthwhile to visit.

Furthermore, the contemporary designed building itself is an highlight. Especially, if you are interested in design and architecture, you should not miss this unique landmark. There is plenty to discover inside and outside.

![MPlus Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "World-class M+ Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong")

The world class MPlus Museum

So, if you have visited MoMA in New York or the Tate Modern in London, you will enjoy and love this museum. In fact, this world-class museum doesn’t need to hide. Having said that, the M+ Museum is a must-visit and not only a great choice on a rainy day. Expect to stay the whole day.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

The M+ is located at the West Kowloon Cultural District (WKCD). The area is a vibrant hub of the local and international art scene.

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

![Follow the signs to get to the Mplus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Sign leading to the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Another option is to leave the Kowloon MTR station through Exit E4 or E5. Walk along Nga Cheung Road. Then cross the footbridge and follow the signs to the museum.

## Is it worthwhile to visit the M+ Museum?

The M+ Museum is highly recommended not only if you love or are interested in modern art, design and architecture. Focusing on various disciplines as well as having thematic collections such as e.g. Hong Kong’s visual culture makes this museum a must-visit.

![Hong Kong MPlus Museum is not only a popular place to visit for modern art lovers](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The M+ Museum is a must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong")

Enjoy the architecture of the museum and stunning harbour views

The large collections are very well curated. Interactive exhibits, latest technologies (e.g. use mobile devices to interact with the collections), M+ Playscape, the gigantic outdoor LED screen all add to the overall experience and make it worthwhile to visit.

Furthermore, the contemporary designed building itself is an highlight. Especially, if you are interested in design and architecture, you should not miss this unique landmark. There is plenty to discover inside and outside.

![MPlus Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "World-class M+ Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong")

The world class MPlus Museum

So, if you have visited MoMA in New York or the Tate Modern in London, you will enjoy and love this museum. In fact, this world-class museum doesn’t need to hide. Having said that, the M+ Museum is a must-visit and not only a great choice on a rainy day. Expect to stay the whole day.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

## Where is the location of the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The M+ is located at the West Kowloon Cultural District (WKCD). The area is a vibrant hub of the local and international art scene.

![Hong Kong Mplus Museum and the West Kowloon Cultural District are not too far away from the popular Xiqu Centre](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The Xiqu Centre is located close to and M+ Museum")

Xiqu Centre is located in close proximity

There are several arts venues and cultural facilities. All of them offer world-class exhibitions, arts, performances and cultural events. Having said that the location of the museum makes it easy to combine several attractions at once.

![Hong Kong M+ Museum is situated at the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The Lyric Theatre Complex is constructed just next to the MPlus Museum")

Lyric Theatre Complex is constructed just next to the MPlus

Next to the M+ Museum is the Palace Museum, Art Park, Freespace, Xiqu Centre and the upcoming Lyric Theatre Complex. On the way to or from the museum, you can also visit another popular sightseeing attraction.

![The sky100 Observation Deck next to the MPlus Museum is another popular sightseeing attraction at the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Close to the museum is the sky100 Observation Deck inside the ICC building")

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

![Follow the signs to get to the Mplus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Sign leading to the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Sign leading the way

Another option is to leave the Kowloon MTR station through Exit E4 or E5. Walk along Nga Cheung Road. Then cross the footbridge and follow the signs to the museum.

![The MPlus Museum can be reached via the harbour crossing footbridge](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "To reach the Hong Kong M+ Museum you have to cross the footbridge")

Cross the footbridge

### By MTR then use free shuttle bus

Alternatively, you can take the MTR subway and travel to the Austin MTR station and take Exit D. From there you can hop on the free shuttle bus taking you to the museum district. The free shuttle bus departs every 20 minutes.

### Where to buy admission tickets?

In general, both types of admission tickets are available from the official ticket counter of the museum as well as through internet online booking platforms.

#### From Official Ticket Counter

General admission tickets as well as tickets for the Special Thematic Exhibition galleries can be purchased directly from the official ticket counters of the museum.

In case you plan to purchase tickets directly at the counter, be aware that you might have to wait long times in line. This attraction is very popular. And it is not unusual to see visitors queuing up hours before the official opening hours of the museum.

In order to avoid disappointment try to purchase and secure your entrance tickets in advance. This can be done through one of the following official online booking platforms.

#### From Online Booking Platforms

The M+ Museum cooperates with several big online booking platforms such as e.g. Cityline, China Travel Service (CTS), Fliggy, Ctrip, Trip.com, Klook and KKDay.

China Travel Service (CTS), Fliggy, Ctrip and Trip.com cater mainly to Chinese tourists. Klook and KKDay offer discounted tickets to the rest of foreign travellers.

Booking through one of the platforms has the several advantages. First, you can immediately see which days are sold out. Second, you can immediately secure your preferred day of visit (instant confirmation). Third, booking from the online discount providers entitles the visitors with direct admission. And lastly, don’t forget to check tickets for other sightseeing attractions. These platforms provide discounted admission tickets to all kind of attractions.

## Is it worthwhile to visit the M+ Museum?

The M+ Museum is highly recommended not only if you love or are interested in modern art, design and architecture. Focusing on various disciplines as well as having thematic collections such as e.g. Hong Kong’s visual culture makes this museum a must-visit.

![Hong Kong MPlus Museum is not only a popular place to visit for modern art lovers](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The M+ Museum is a must-visit sightseeing attraction in Hong Kong")

Enjoy the architecture of the museum and stunning harbour views

The large collections are very well curated. Interactive exhibits, latest technologies (e.g. use mobile devices to interact with the collections), M+ Playscape, the gigantic outdoor LED screen all add to the overall experience and make it worthwhile to visit.

Furthermore, the contemporary designed building itself is an highlight. Especially, if you are interested in design and architecture, you should not miss this unique landmark. There is plenty to discover inside and outside.

![MPlus Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "World-class M+ Museum at the West Kowloon Cultural District in Hong Kong")

The world class MPlus Museum

So, if you have visited MoMA in New York or the Tate Modern in London, you will enjoy and love this museum. In fact, this world-class museum doesn’t need to hide. Having said that, the M+ Museum is a must-visit and not only a great choice on a rainy day. Expect to stay the whole day.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

![Follow the signs to get to the Mplus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Sign leading to the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Sign leading the way

Another option is to leave the Kowloon MTR station through Exit E4 or E5. Walk along Nga Cheung Road. Then cross the footbridge and follow the signs to the museum.

![The MPlus Museum can be reached via the harbour crossing footbridge](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "To reach the Hong Kong M+ Museum you have to cross the footbridge")

Cross the footbridge

### By MTR then use free shuttle bus

Alternatively, you can take the MTR subway and travel to the Austin MTR station and take Exit D. From there you can hop on the free shuttle bus taking you to the museum district. The free shuttle bus departs every 20 minutes.

![Take Exit D at MTR Austin station to enjoy free shuttle bus service to the MPlus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Free shuttle bus service to Hong Kong M+ Museum from MTR Austin Station Exit D")

MTR notice for free shuttle bus at Exit D

![Enjoy free shuttle bus service to the MPlus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Free circular shuttle bus service to Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Free circular shuttle bus

In case you don’t want to wait or would like to enjoy a walk then you can the Exit B4 or B5. The walk towards the museum is approx. 15-20 minutes.

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

## Where is the location of the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The M+ is located at the West Kowloon Cultural District (WKCD). The area is a vibrant hub of the local and international art scene.

![Hong Kong Mplus Museum and the West Kowloon Cultural District are not too far away from the popular Xiqu Centre](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The Xiqu Centre is located close to and M+ Museum")

Xiqu Centre is located in close proximity

There are several arts venues and cultural facilities. All of them offer world-class exhibitions, arts, performances and cultural events. Having said that the location of the museum makes it easy to combine several attractions at once.

![Hong Kong M+ Museum is situated at the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "The Lyric Theatre Complex is constructed just next to the MPlus Museum")

Lyric Theatre Complex is constructed just next to the MPlus

Next to the M+ Museum is the Palace Museum, Art Park, Freespace, Xiqu Centre and the upcoming Lyric Theatre Complex. On the way to or from the museum, you can also visit another popular sightseeing attraction.

![The sky100 Observation Deck next to the MPlus Museum is another popular sightseeing attraction at the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Close to the museum is the sky100 Observation Deck inside the ICC building")

The museum is close to the sky100 Observation Deck inside the ICC

The [sky100 Observation Deck](https://www.nextstophongkong.com/sky100-hong-kong-observation-deck-icc/ "sky100 Observation Deck - Hong Kong's highest indoor observation deck inside the ICC building") – the highest indoor observation deck – is inside the ICC (the city’s highest building) and connected with the [ELEMENTS shopping mall](https://www.nextstophongkong.com/elements/ "ELEMENTS Shopping Mall - Hong Kong's best shopping malls in Kowloon").

![Enjoy additional art performances and exhibition at the Freespace venue at the West Kowloon Cultural District](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Another art and cultural hub is the Freespace venue next to the M+ Museum Hong Kong")

Freespace venue is next to the museum

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

![Follow the signs to get to the Mplus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Sign leading to the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Sign leading the way

Another option is to leave the Kowloon MTR station through Exit E4 or E5. Walk along Nga Cheung Road. Then cross the footbridge and follow the signs to the museum.

![The MPlus Museum can be reached via the harbour crossing footbridge](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "To reach the Hong Kong M+ Museum you have to cross the footbridge")

Cross the footbridge

### By MTR then use free shuttle bus

Alternatively, you can take the MTR subway and travel to the Austin MTR station and take Exit D. From there you can hop on the free shuttle bus taking you to the museum district. The free shuttle bus departs every 20 minutes.

![Take Exit D at MTR Austin station to enjoy free shuttle bus service to the MPlus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Free shuttle bus service to Hong Kong M+ Museum from MTR Austin Station Exit D")

MTR notice for free shuttle bus at Exit D

![Enjoy free shuttle bus service to the MPlus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Free circular shuttle bus service to Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Free circular shuttle bus

In case you don’t want to wait or would like to enjoy a walk then you can the Exit B4 or B5. The walk towards the museum is approx. 15-20 minutes.

## What are the Opening Hours and when is it the best time to visit the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

The official opening hours of the Hong Kong M+ Museum are:

* 10:00am – 6:00pm (Tues – Thu, and weekends)
* 10:00am – 10:00pm (Fri)

The museum is closed on Mondays. The museum is open on all public holidays unless it fall on a Monday.

So, when is the best time to visit? It is always a good idea to plan ahead if you want to visit this attraction. The museum is very popular among travel agencies, teachers and students. Expect large crowds. Therefore, try to [purchase and secure your entrance tickets](#online "purchase ticket of M+ Museum online") in advance to avoid disappointment.

Besides, it is recommended to avoid weekends and public holidays. Similar to other attractions it can get crowded. Having said that, the best time to visit is during the week.

## How to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum?

You can get to M+ Museum by subway and then walk or use free shuttle bus service.

### By MTR then walk

The most convenient way to get to the Hong Kong M+ Museum is to take Hong Kong’s MTR. Take the subway to the Kowloon MTR Station and take Exit C1 or D1 (these subway exits are closest to the museum). Follow the signs to the Artist Square Bridge and cross it. Then follow the signs towards the museum. It’s an approx. 10 minutes walk.

![Follow the signs to get to the Mplus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Sign leading to the Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Sign leading the way

Another option is to leave the Kowloon MTR station through Exit E4 or E5. Walk along Nga Cheung Road. Then cross the footbridge and follow the signs to the museum.

![The MPlus Museum can be reached via the harbour crossing footbridge](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "To reach the Hong Kong M+ Museum you have to cross the footbridge")

Cross the footbridge

### By MTR then use free shuttle bus

Alternatively, you can take the MTR subway and travel to the Austin MTR station and take Exit D. From there you can hop on the free shuttle bus taking you to the museum district. The free shuttle bus departs every 20 minutes.

![Take Exit D at MTR Austin station to enjoy free shuttle bus service to the MPlus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Free shuttle bus service to Hong Kong M+ Museum from MTR Austin Station Exit D")

MTR notice for free shuttle bus at Exit D

![Enjoy free shuttle bus service to the MPlus Museum Hong Kong](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20620%20413%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27620%27%20height%3D%27413%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E "Free circular shuttle bus service to Hong Kong M+ Museum")

Free circular shuttle bus

In case you don’t want to wait or would like to enjoy a walk then you can the Exit B4 or B5. The walk towards the museum is approx. 15-20 minutes.

Free circular shuttle bus

## FAQs: How to Take the Hong Kong Airport Express

* ### Where can I get on the Airport Express in Hong Kong?

  You can board at Hong Kong Station, Kowloon Station, Tsing Yi Station, or Airport Station. All are clearly signposted and connected to the MTR system.
* ### Is the in-town check-in process free?

  Indeed. accessible at Kowloon and Hong Kong stations. Simply bring your ticket and passport, and check in 90 to 120 minutes prior to departure.
* ### Is Airport Express superior to a taxi or bus?

  more dependable and quicker than busses less expensive than taxis at rush hour includes a complimentary shuttle to well-known hotels.

# Welcome to The Ritz-Carlton, Hong Kong

## TIMELESS JOURNEY IN THE SKY

The Ritz-Carlton, Hong Kong stands majestically in Tsim Sha Tsui, within the vibrant West Kowloon District. Perched atop the International Commerce Centre and Elements Shopping Mall, the hotel is just steps from notable cultural landmarks such as M+ and Hong Kong Palace Museum, as well as the Kai Tak Stadium for concerts and world-class events. With convenient access to the High-Speed Railway Station and Airport Express, reaching the airport in just 21 minutes. Occupying floors 106 to 118, all rooms and suites feature breathtaking views of the Hong Kong skyline and Victoria Harbour from 490 meters above sea level. The hotel boasts five dining venues, including Michelin-starred dining experience from authentic Cantonese cuisine at Tin Lung Heen, innovative Italian fine dining at Tosca di Angelo, exquisite lunch and dinner buffet at Café 103, delightful afternoon tea at The Lounge and Bar, and lively nightlife at Ozone on level 118.
